frame: Lunar Mean-Earth/Polar-Axis (ME, DE421-aligned); planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude

overview.projection: south polar stereographic, sphere 1737.4 km, +y toward lon 0, +x toward lon 90E; image row 0 = +y edge
overview.note: Shaded relief with a fixed artificial light direction; display only, not a physical illumination state.

sites.name: Mons Mouton — IM-2 Athena landing site
sites.coord_note: As-landed position of Intuitive Machines IM-2 'Athena' (CLPS PRIME-1 delivery, 2025-03-06) reported by the LROC team: 84.7906°S, 29.1957°E. NASA's CP-22 delivery (Intuitive Machines IM-4) also targets Mons Mouton, but NASA has published no CP-22 coordinates; this point is NOT a CP-22 landing target.
sites.elevation_source: Bilinear sample of LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ.TIF at the site coordinates; height above the 1737.4 km sphere [R-LOLA-PGDA]

slope.source: LDSM_80S_80MPP_ADJ.TIF pixel containing the site, and mean of the 3x3 pixels around it [R-LOLA-PGDA]
slope.note: Regional slope over an 80 m pixel; context only, not a landing-hazard assessment.

horizon.layout: float32 little-endian: n_az horizon elevations (deg) followed by n_az distances (m) of the horizon-defining terrain sample; azimuth i*az_step_deg clockwise from north

terrain.layout: float32 little-endian heights (m above the 1737.4 km sphere), row-major [j][i]; node (i,j) lies at local azimuthal-equidistant offsets east = -half + i*spacing, north = -half + j*spacing from the site

sites.name: Malapert A — IM-1 Odysseus landing site

sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge (PGDA Site 01)
sites.coord_note: Representative analysis point chosen by this project: the centre of the 240 m pixel with the highest 18.6-year average solar illumination (Mazarico et al. 2011 map AVGVISIB_65S_240M_201608) inside the footprint of NASA PGDA 'Site01: Connecting ridge'. It is not a mission landing target.

sites.name: Sunlit peak 1 — NASA average-illumination map
sites.coord_note: Representative analysis point chosen by this project, not a mission landing target: the rank-1 local maximum of the NASA 18.6-year average solar-illumination map AVGVISIB_65S_240M_201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011) within 300 km of the pole, at least 25 km from the other analysis points and from higher-ranked peaks. The 240 m map pixel centre is used.
